title: SentencePiece: Language-Independent Tokenization
hook: Most tokenizers assume you can split on spaces first. SentencePiece drops that assumption and tokenizes raw text directly — in any language.
key_points: Operates on raw text with no language-specific pre-tokenization step.
Treats whitespace as an ordinary character, so tokenization is fully reversible.
Language-independent, which helps with scripts that don't separate words by spaces.
Widely used to tokenize large language models.
content_html: Kudo and Richardson built SentencePiece, a tokenizer that works directly on raw text without a separate, language-specific pre-tokenization step. By treating spaces as ordinary characters, it stays language-independent and fully reversible — you can reconstruct the exact original text from the tokens. It's widely used to tokenize large language models.
extra_html:
How it works

Many tokenizers first split text on whitespace and only then apply subword rules, which quietly assumes the language uses spaces between words. SentencePiece skips that assumption: it consumes the raw character stream, encodes spaces as a special marker so they're preserved, and learns subword units (using algorithms such as byte-pair encoding or a unigram language model) over that stream. Because nothing is thrown away or guessed at, decoding the tokens reproduces the original text exactly.

Why it matters

Languages like Japanese, Chinese, and Thai don't put spaces between words, so space-based pre-tokenization breaks down for them. Handling raw text directly makes SentencePiece work consistently across languages and removes brittle, language-specific preprocessing from the pipeline. Its reversibility and self-contained design made it a convenient, reliable choice for training many modern models.

flashcards.prompt: How does SentencePiece achieve language independence?
flashcards.back_html: It operates on raw text with no whitespace-based pre-tokenization, treating spaces as ordinary characters via a special marker.

flashcards.prompt: Why does SentencePiece treat whitespace as an ordinary character?

choices.text: So tokenization is fully reversible - the exact original text can be reconstructed
To make the vocabulary larger and more expressive
Because spaces are the most frequent token to merge

flashcards.explanation_html: Encoding spaces as a marker means nothing is thrown away, so decoding the tokens reproduces the original text exactly.

choices.text: Languages like Japanese, Chinese, and Thai that don't separate words with spaces
Languages with very large alphabets like Russian

flashcards.explanation_html: Scripts without spaces between words defeat whitespace pre-tokenization; SentencePiece's raw-text approach handles them.
